#### General Tab

The General tab in the Meter Editor shows basic information about the meter, such as where it is located and what Close Group it belongs to. The fields that are shaded in gray such as Meter Type and Meter Direction are read-only and are retrieved from the meter’s characteristics. These read-only fields are editable in the Volume Editor.

By default, the only fields required to save a new meter are Meter Number and Fluid Phase, and for liquid meters, Operation Type, which is defaulted to Batch.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 498;height: 463;" />

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Data Field Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following items are available on the General tab:

- **Meter Type** - Read-only field that displays the type of meter. This value is retrieved from the meter’s characteristics and can be edited from the Volume Editor or updated during a meter import.

- **Alt. Meter Number** - Informational field used to document an alternate meter number. This typically references a third party or contract meter number.

- **Meter Direction** - Read-only field that displays whether a meter is classified as Inlet, Outlet, Throughput, Balance Check, Transfer, Tieover, or Off System for balancing purposes. This value is retrieved from the meter’s characteristics and can be edited from the Volume Editor.

- **Customer** - The customer the meter belongs to. This name can be printed on reports if enabled under the **[**Reports** tab](Reports%20Tab.md)**.

- **Cust. Meter Number** - Informational field used to document the customer's meter number.

- **Check Meter Exists** - Specifies whether an existing check meter is associated to the meter; commonly used if data from another meter is being measured at the same measurement point.

- **Helium Meter**\* - Designates whether a meter is a helium meter. If "Yes" is selected, FLOWCAL will calculate the following:

  - Total net helium
  - Gross 50% to 65% helium
  - Net 50% to 65% helium
  - Gross less than 50% helium
  - Net less than 50% helium

  These calculation results will be stored in user-defined fields 1 through 5 for meter periodic records. The Meter Rollups service will always sum user-defined fields 1 through 5 in the meter periodic values, regardless of the rollup action configured for those fields (**Settings Manager** \> **Custom Fields** \> **Meter Periodic Values** tab).

- **Account for DST**\* - Indicates whether to compensate for Daylight Saving Time. If "Yes" is selected, the DST time change table is used to establish when to adjust for time changes to avoid generating missing data exceptions and duplicate data and/or high periodic flow time exceptions.

- **Close Groups** - Only visible if the close schedule type is set to "Close Group" in the FLOWCAL Configuration screen.

- **Fluid Phase** - Defines the meter phase conditions as gas or liquid; the fluid phase is defined on meter creation and cannot be changed once the meter is created.

- **Meter Status** - Indicates whether the meter is active; pulled from meter’s characteristics and applicable to the current system time (all other meter characteristic values displayed on other tabs are applicable to the last meter periodic record).

- **Fluid Service** - Defines the meter fluid service as "Hydrocarbon" (default) or "Nonhydrocarbon" for liquid meters. The fluid service is specified when creating a new liquid meter and cannot be changed once the meter is created.

- **Business Status** - The current or proposed meter status that can be influenced by test reports from TESTit. This status is not datetime effective and can be updated manually via the Meter Editor or, when mapped, TESTit imports. This status overrides the Meter Status.

  Meters that have a business status other than "On" are treated as out of service and will not import data or be included when running reports for a list.

- **System** - Informational field that indicates which system the meter is assigned to, typically set during meter creation.

- **Notes** - Additional notes about the meter; up to 320 characters.

  The notes stored on the General tab are only available from the Meter Editor. Right-click the Meter Editor screen to add or view notes that can be accessed throughout the application (e.g., from the Volume Editor). If additional notes are needed, click the **Notes** button in the right side of the form for an additional 2,000 characters.

- **City** - City the meter is in; up to 50 characters.

- **County** - County the meter is in; up to 20 characters; options are defined in the County Editor.

- **State** - State the meter is in; up to 50 characters; options are defined in the State Editor.

- **Country** - Country the meter is in; up to 50 characters; options are defined in the Country Editor.

- **Time Zone** - Time zone the meter is in; up to 80 characters; options are defined in the Time Zone Editor.

When a time zone is selected for a meter and the Time Zone Shift in enabled on the Imports tab, dates contained in the import data will be adjusted according to the offset associated to the time zone.

- **Quarter** - Each section is divided into quarter sections, which are each further divided into quarter sections, for a total of 16 parts per section; up to 25 characters.

  "NW 1/4 of the SE 1/4" refers to the northwestern-most quarter of the southeastern quarter.

  

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 125;height: 123;" />

  </div>

  </div>
- **Section** - The basic unit of a township and range; each section refers to an area of a square mile; up to three characters.
- **Township** - A measure of the distance north or south from the baseline, six miles in length; up to four characters.
- **Range** - A measure of the distance east or west from the principal meridian, six miles in length; up to four characters.
- **Meridian** - A geographical north to south reference point; up to 25 characters.
- **Latitude** - A geographic coordinate specifying a north-south location on the Earth’s surface, measured from the Equator; up to 12 characters.
- **Longitude** - A geographic coordinate specifying an east-west location on the Earth’s surface, measured from the Prime Meridian; up to 12 characters.

**\***Not available for dead oil meters or flash gas meters.

</div>
